Six of nine lines are predicted to better than $1.3\,\%$ and the two core lines to $0.1\,\%$; the three worst are the $z$ valence lines, whose residuals are $7\times10^{-7}$ to $1.8\times10^{-6}$ in absolute terms, at the level of the transform's own rectangle-rule bias. The $\gamma^4$ law itself is the sharpest single confirmation: on the $y$ line at $0.702205382$ the bias fell from $+2.3432\times10^{-3}$ at $\tau=50$ to $+6.745\times10^{-5}$ at $\tau=125$, a factor $34.7$ against the predicted $(125/50)^4=39.06$, while the two core lines, which have no near neighbour in their own polarisation, did not move at all ($6.0393\times10^{-3}$ at both $\tau$, ratio $1.00$) — exactly as a $\gamma^4/\Delta^3$ bias with $\Delta\to\infty$ must behave. The long run also confirms the selection rule at higher resolution: the $x$ core window peaks nowhere above $\operatorname{Im}\alpha=2.9\times10^{-8}$.

**MEASURED · amplitudes, not only positions.** Two checks that no peak finder can fake. First, the Thouless f-sum rule for RPA: the energy deposited by the impulse is $E(0^+)-E_\text{RHF}=\kappa^2\sum_k\omega_kz_k^2$ with the oracle's own RPA roots and transition dipoles. Predicted and measured, identical for every $\Delta t$ and integrator: $x$, $4.890464\times10^{-9}$ against $4.889969\times10^{-9}$ (relative $1.0\times10^{-4}$, the absolute residue being $5\times10^{-13}$); $y$, $1.821601\times10^{-6}$ against $1.821600\times10^{-6}$ (relative $4.3\times10^{-7}$); $z$, $1.090696\times10^{-6}$ against $1.090695\times10^{-6}$ (relative $5.1\times10^{-7}$). No transform is involved in this one. Second, the seven valence $\operatorname{Im}\alpha$ peak heights against the Lemma 4 model with the oracle's $z_k$: relative agreement $6.5\times10^{-6}$ to $1.6\times10^{-4}$, for heights spanning $0.506$ to $97.95$. Position, amplitude and absorbed energy are all the RPA spectrum.

**MEASURED · second order, separately in the two windows.** Ratios of $\sup_\omega\lvert\operatorname{Im}\alpha_{\Delta t}-\operatorname{Im}\alpha_{\Delta t/2}\rvert$ over each window, and of the worst peak-position error:

| family | window | pol. | $\sup\Delta\operatorname{Im}\alpha$ ratios | peak-error ratios |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Magnus-2 $0.02\!\to\!0.01\!\to\!0.005$ | valence | $x$ / $y$ / $z$ | $4.01$ / $4.01$ / $3.99$ | $3.92,3.69$ ($x$) |
| Magnus-2 | core | $y$ / $z$ | $3.48$ / $3.57$ | $3.97,3.99$ / $3.97,4.00$ |
| MMUT $0.01\!\to\!0.005\!\to\!0.0025$ | valence | $x$ / $y$ / $z$ | $4.00$ / $4.00$ / $3.99$ | $3.69,3.05$ ($x$) |
| MMUT | core | $y$ / $z$ | $3.96$ / $3.97$ | $3.99,4.00$ / $4.00,4.01$ |

The answer to Sol's question 4 is yes: second order in both windows for both integrators. Three qualifications, all measured. The Magnus-2 core ratios $3.48$ and $3.57$ are below four because $\Delta t=0.02$ gives $\omega_{\max}\Delta t=0.42$, outside the asymptotic regime; the MMUT core ratios, whose coarsest step is $0.01$, are $3.96$ and $3.97$. The valence peak-error ratios are only meaningful where the $\Delta t$ error dominates the $\gamma^4$ bias of Lemma 4 — for the $z$ lines at $1.0466$ and $1.4617$ the two are comparable and the error changes sign between $\Delta t=0.01$ and $0.005$, which is why their ratios read $0.50$ and $0.87$ rather than $4$; the window bias is not a function of $\Delta t$ at all. And MMUT at $\Delta t$ reproduces Magnus-2 at the same $\Delta t$ to six digits in every peak, which is the expected coincidence of two time-symmetric second-order schemes at these step sizes, not independent confirmation.

**MEASURED · the invariants.** $\operatorname{Tr}P$ ends at $10.000000000047$ after $30{,}000$ steps, $10.000000000094$ after $60{,}000$, $10.000000000189$ after $120{,}000$: the excess is linear in the step count at $1.6\times10^{-15}$ per step, which is $\approx n\varepsilon$. Idempotency defect $1.0\times10^{-11}$ to $2.4\times10^{-10}$, growing the same way. $\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Tr}P\le2.5\times10^{-14}$ throughout. Field-free energy drift over $600$ a.u.: Magnus-2 $-3.96\times10^{-8}$, $-6.29\times10^{-9}$, $-1.71\times10^{-9}$ at $\Delta t=0.02,0.01,0.005$ ($y$ kick; ratios $6.3$ and $3.7$, between second and third order, consistent with the ports document's measured ratio $8$ on H₂ but not as clean); MMUT $-3.5\times10^{-10}$, $-4.9\times10^{-10}$, $-9.6\times10^{-10}$, which is rounding accumulation rather than discretisation and is $18$ times smaller than Magnus-2 at the same $\Delta t=0.01$.

**REFUTED · Corollary 2.1 of the ports document.** [research/MATH-CHRONUSQ-PORTS-2026-09-11.md](MATH-CHRONUSQ-PORTS-2026-09-11.md) states "A drift of $\operatorname{Tr}(DS)$ under any unitary integrator is a defect of $S^{\pm1/2}$, never of the integrator." Corrected line: a drift of $\operatorname{Tr}(DS)$ is a defect of $S^{\pm1/2}$, or the accumulated rounding of the similarity products, never of the integrator's mathematics. The measured drift here is the second kind: it is zero at $t=0$ (so $S^{\pm1/2}$ is exact to $5\times10^{-16}$) and grows linearly at $1.6\times10^{-15}$ per step, reaching $1.9\times10^{-10}$ at $120{,}000$ steps — invisible on the ports document's 1600-step H₂ fixture, where the same rate predicts $2.6\times10^{-12}$ against its reported $3.6\times10^{-13}$.

#### 6 · Judgements

**REFUTED · Sol's core timestep law.** Sol writes "Sampling requires $\Delta t<\pi/\omega_{\max}\approx0.157$ a.u. $=3.80$ as … $\theta=0.2$ gives $\Delta t\le0.010$ a.u. $=0.242$ as and about $31$ samples per core cycle." Every number is $\omega_{\max}=20$ where the measured value is not $20$. Corrected lines: the largest occupied–virtual orbital gap is $\varepsilon_7-\varepsilon_1=20.983461$, and the highest frequency actually present in the linear-response dipole trace is the largest RPA root, $20.157421877$; so the sampling bound is $\pi/20.983461=0.149718$ a.u. $=3.622$ as for the density's coherences and $\pi/20.157422=0.155853$ for the trace, both below Sol's $0.157$, which is therefore not a bound. $\theta=0.2$ gives $\Delta t\le0.2/20.983461=0.0095312$, not $0.010$; conversely $\Delta t=0.010$ is $\theta=0.20983$. The core cycle is $2\pi/20.983461=0.299442$ a.u., which is $29.94$ samples at $\Delta t=0.010$ and $31.42$ at $\Delta t=0.0095312$: "$31$ samples" belongs to the corrected step, not to $0.010$.

**REFUTED · Sol's MMUT change.** Sol writes "For the same phase cap use $2\omega_{\max}\Delta t\le\theta$, hence $\Delta t\le0.005$ a.u. for $\theta=0.2$." Corrected line: MMUT needs no tightening relative to Magnus-2 at these step sizes, because its leading error coefficient is the same. MEASURED ([scratch/richardson.py](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/richardson.py)): writing $\omega_\text{peak}(\Delta t)=\omega_\text{RPA}+\delta_\text{window}+C\Delta t^2$, the constant window bias cancels in successive differences, and the ratios $\lvert\omega(\Delta t)-\omega(\Delta t/2)\rvert/\lvert\omega(\Delta t/2)-\omega(\Delta t/4)\rvert$ are $3.967$ to $4.003$ for all nine bright lines in both families — clean second order, in the valence window and in the core window alike. The fitted $C$ agrees between the two integrators to four digits: $0.0620$ and $0.0620$ for the $x$ line, $60.358$ and $60.493$ for the $y$ core line, $53.390$ and $53.496$ for the $z$ core line. Sol's "parasitic parity mode" was not excited at any step tried, but `lab/density.js` restarts MMUT with a Magnus-2 step every $50$ steps, so this is not a test of unrestarted MMUT.

**DERIVED-HERE and MEASURED · the timestep law that replaces it.** The honest law is per-line, with an accuracy target, and it is set by the core:
$$ \lvert\omega_\text{peak}-\omega_\text{RPA}-\delta_\text{window}\rvert=C\,\Delta t^2,\qquad C\in[0.062,\,0.314]\ \text{for the seven valence lines},\qquad C\in[53.4,\,60.5]\ \text{for the two O }1s\text{ lines}. $$
Hence $\Delta t\le\sqrt{\text{target}/C}$: a valence line to $10^{-5}$ needs $\Delta t\le5.6\times10^{-3}$ ($\theta=0.12$), a core line to $10^{-4}$ needs $\Delta t\le1.29\times10^{-3}$ ($\theta=0.027$), and Sol's $\theta=0.2$ delivers $2.9\times10^{-5}$ on the valence lines but only $5.5\times10^{-3}$ on the core lines. The spread of $C$ between the two windows is a factor $170$–$980$ while $\omega$ spreads only $42$, so $C$ is not $\omega^3/24$ (which would give $341$ for the core and $0.0047$ for the $x$ line, wrong in both directions); what sets it is Question 9. Practical consequence for the instrument: if the O $1s$ line is on screen, the timestep is seven times smaller than Sol's law says, and the run is seven times longer.

**CERTIFIED · Sol's "what the law is not".** "Magnus-2 is norm-, trace-, and idempotency-preserving for any $\Delta t$, so the core scale is not a stability bound." MEASURED at $\Delta t=0.02$, which is $\theta=0.42$, twice Sol's cap: $\operatorname{Tr}P=10.000000000047$, idempotency defect $1.0\times10^{-11}$, energy drift $2.3\times10^{-10}$ — a perfectly conserved run whose core peak is wrong by $2.4\times10^{-2}$. This is Corollary 2.2 of the ports document happening on a real molecule.

**MEASURED · the $96^3$ field, judged mathematically only.** $96^3=884{,}736$ voxels and a seven-layer `r32float` cache of $24{,}772{,}608$ bytes $=24.77$ MB $=23.63$ MiB: both of Sol's counts are right. So are "$35$ coefficient multiplies" for the five-occupied-orbital density and "$28$ symmetric AO pairs" for the density-matrix form, $7\cdot8/2=28$. Three corrections, all from [scratch/gpu.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/gpu.mjs).

**REFUTED · "twenty-one primitive exponentials per voxel".** Corrected line: twelve. STO-3G water has four distinct exponent sets, not seven: the oxygen $sp$ shell's three exponents $\{5.033151319,1.169596125,0.38038896\}$ are shared by $2s,2p_x,2p_y,2p_z$, so a voxel needs $3$ (O $1s$) $+\,3$ (O $sp$) $+\,3$ (H) $+\,3$ (H) $=12$ calls to `exp` and three squared distances, not $21$. Sol's figure is $7\times3$, which double-counts the shared shell by $1.75\times$. For benzene the same count is $6\times(3+3)+6\times3=54$, not $36\times3=108$.

**REFUTED · the `rgba16float` argument.** Sol writes "store density in `r32float` because the O-core dynamic range is hostile to `rgba16float`". MEASURED: $\rho=193.3139$ a.u. at the oxygen nucleus, $0.3627$ at a hydrogen nucleus, $0.492165$ at an O–H midpoint, and $1.8\times10^{-28}$ twelve bohr out; the span from the core peak to a $10^{-6}$ display floor is $1.93\times10^{8}$, which `f16` covers comfortably (normals to $6.1\times10^{-5}$, subnormals to $6\times10^{-8}$) at a uniform $4.9\times10^{-4}$ relative step, because it is floating point. Corrected line: store density in `r32float` because a scalar field wastes three of four `rgba16float` channels, and because an `f16` accumulator adding the oxygen $1s$ AO value $\chi=9.6459$ at the nucleus to a $10^{-3}$ valence term loses the latter entirely — the hazard is accumulation, not storage range.

**MEASURED · the culling claim, bounded.** Cull radii at which the conservative envelope $\sum_i\lvert d_i\rvert r^{L}e^{-\alpha_{\min}r^2}$ falls below $10^{-6}$: O $1s$ $1.580$ bohr, O $2s$ $5.978$, each O $2p$ $6.640$, each H $1s$ $8.892$. The union of supports is therefore a region of radius $\approx10.3$ bohr about the hydrogens, so a grid box sized to hold it is a cube of side $\approx20.6$ bohr and the culled fraction is at most $1-\pi/6=47.6\,\%$. Sol's "workgroups outside all seven supports write zero without exponentials" is correct but buys under a factor of two at this threshold, and nothing at all if the box is fitted to the molecule instead of to the diffuse hydrogen tail.

**MEASURED · where the cache actually pays.** For H₂O the per-voxel choice is $12$ transcendentals plus $21$ contraction fused multiply-adds (direct) against $7$ texture fetches plus $28$ pair products (cached): on the project's RTX 3070 an `exp` is quarter-rate, so the direct route costs $\approx48$ arithmetic slots against $\approx56$ for the cached route plus $28$ B per voxel of bandwidth, which is $24.8$ MB per frame and $1.49$ GB/s at $60$ fps against the card's $448$ GB/s. The AO cache is therefore roughly break-even for water and is justified by the ladder, not by water: benzene needs $54$ transcendentals per voxel direct, against $36$ fetches and $36\cdot37/2=666$ pair products, which is $1.18$ Gflop per frame and $70.7$ Gflop/s at $60$ fps — trivial arithmetic, but a $36$-layer cache is $127.4$ MB, so at the ceiling of Sol's own ladder the binding constraint is memory, not flops, and the cache must become tiled or single-precision-packed.

**UNVERIFIED (build items, not proofs) · Sol's questions 5 and 6.** Question 5 asks for a browser GPU benchmark of the AO cache at $96^3$ on target hardware. That is a measurement of a program that does not exist yet; the mathematics above says what it should find (break-even at seven AOs, decisive at thirty-six, memory-bound at the ceiling), but upload, cache-build and frame times are properties of a shader and a driver and cannot be proved. Question 6 asks for a save–restore–save fixture with a deliberately wrong basis hash and an MMUT record missing $P(t-\Delta t)$, and for the exact rejection messages. Exact strings are an implementation decision; there is no theorem to prove and no number to measure until the record exists. Both are build items. What this round can add to them is the content of the validation, not its wording: on restore, check $\operatorname{Tr}(DS)=N_e$ to $n\varepsilon$ times the step count already taken (the measured drift law $1.6\times10^{-15}$ per step), reject a `mmut` record without $P(t-\Delta t)$ and parity, and recompute the basis hash over the BSE decimal strings, not over parsed doubles.

#### 7 · Close

**Killed, with the corrected line.** (1) Round 0's "$E=-74.963023138$" and the commission's "$1\,\text{Å}=1.8897261246$ bohr, PySCF's value" → $-74.963023162862$ on the pinned BSE decimals, and $1/0.52917721092=1.8897261245650618$; PySCF's internal STO-3G table is truncated to eight digits and accounts for $2.5\times10^{-8}$ of energy and $4.3\times10^{-6}$ of $V$. (2) Sol's "For $t\ge44$, use $F_m(t)=\frac{(2m-1)!!\sqrt\pi}{2^{m+1}t^{m+1/2}}$" → correct for $m\le4$ ($4.08\times10^{-15}$ measured against Sol's own $4.1\times10^{-15}$ estimate) but wrong by three orders at $m=8$ ($1.408\times10^{-11}$), which the ledger's $l\le2$ design reaches; replace with $F_0=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2\sqrt t}$ and upward recursion (Proposition 9, $7.19\times10^{-16}$), or move the switch to $t\ge52.6$. #### Answers 7–12

**DERIVED-HERE · 7, exact-kernel deblending.** Replace peak-by-peak correction by a global variable-projection fit to the exact kernel used by the sampled transform. For $t_n=n h$, $n=1,\ldots,M-1$, $q=e^{-\gamma h}$, define
$$
I_M(x)=h\sum_{n=1}^{M-1}q^n\cos(xnh),\qquad K_M(\omega,\Omega)=I_M(\omega-\Omega)-I_M(\omega+\Omega).
$$
Then a linear-response trace $\delta\mu_n=2\kappa\sum_{k=1}^N A_k\sin(\Omega_kt_n)$ gives the code's transform exactly as $y_r=\sum_kA_kK_M(\omega_r,\Omega_k)$: neighbour overlap, the negative-frequency image, the finite endpoint $T$, exponential damping, and the rectangle rule are all inside $K_M$, with no asymptotic truncation.

**DERIVED-HERE · 7, estimator.** For trial ordered frequencies $0<\Omega_1<\cdots<\Omega_N<\pi/h$, solve the linear nonnegative least-squares problem for $A_k$, then minimise the reduced residual over $\Omega_k$; initialise from the local peaks but report the fitted poles, not the maxima. Expanding this exact normal equation for $T\to\infty$, $\gamma/\lvert\Omega_j-\Omega_k\rvert\to0$ returns Lemma 4 as its first nonzero term, so the fit is its all-orders completion rather than another correction series.

**DERIVED-HERE · 7, bound.** Scale the parameter columns, let $J$ be the fitted model's Jacobian, $\sigma=\sigma_{\min}(J)$, and let $L_J$ bound the Jacobian's Lipschitz constant in the ordered-frequency basin. If the weighted transform residual has norm $\epsilon\le\sigma^2/(8L_J)$, the local least-squares solution obeys
$$
\lVert\widehat\theta-\theta\rVert_2\le\frac{4\epsilon}{\sigma}.
$$
Indeed, Taylor's theorem gives $\lVert f(\theta+d)-f(\theta)\rVert\ge(\sigma-L_J\lVert d\rVert/2)\lVert d\rVert$, while optimality bounds the model displacement by $2\epsilon$. At $T/\tau=12$ the endpoint is not an error because it is present in $K_M$; after retaining frequency coordinates in hartree and scaling the amplitude columns, $4\epsilon/\sigma<10^{-7}$ certifies every fitted frequency to $10^{-7}$, and otherwise the instrument must lengthen the trace or decline the precision claim.

**DERIVED-HERE · 8, linearised operators.** At the stationary RHF density $P_0$, put $\mathcal A X=-i[F_0,X]$, $\mathcal B X=-i[(\partial F/\partial P)X,P_0]$, and $\mathcal L=\mathcal A+\mathcal B$. Expanding the exact frozen-Fock exponentials through $h^3$ gives modified generators $\mathcal L+h^2\mathcal D+O(h^4)$ with
$$
\mathcal D_{\rm M2}=\frac{\mathcal A\mathcal B\mathcal A+\mathcal A\mathcal B^2+\mathcal B\mathcal A^2+\mathcal B\mathcal A\mathcal B}{12}-\frac{\mathcal B^2\mathcal A+\mathcal B^3}{6},
$$
$$
\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}=\frac{\mathcal A\mathcal B\mathcal A+\mathcal A\mathcal B^2}{3}-\frac{\mathcal B\mathcal A^2+\mathcal B\mathcal A\mathcal B+\mathcal B^2\mathcal A+\mathcal B^3}{6}.
$$

**DERIVED-HERE · 8, stencil independence of the line positions.** Their difference is
$$
\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}-\mathcal D_{\rm M2}=\tfrac14[\mathcal A,\mathcal B]\mathcal L=\tfrac14[\mathcal A,\mathcal L]\mathcal L.
$$
For a left/right RPA eigenpair $\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal L=\lambda_j\ell_j^\dagger$, $\mathcal Lr_j=\lambda_jr_j$, its projection vanishes: $\ell_j^\dagger[\mathcal A,\mathcal L]\mathcal Lr_j=0$. Thus both stencils have the same leading eigenvalue and frequency error, even though the $O(h^2)$ mode shapes differ. A Magnus restart can control MMUT's parasitic branch, but it is not the cause of the common $C$; unrestarted MMUT remains the required stability test.

**DERIVED-HERE · 9, what sets $C$.** With $\lambda_j=-i\omega_j$ and $\ell_j^\dagger r_j=1$, the proposed a priori coefficient is
$$
C_j=-\operatorname{Im}\!\left(\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal D_{\rm M2}r_j\right)=-\operatorname{Im}\!\left(\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}r_j\right).
$$
$\mathcal A$ contains the occupied–virtual orbital gaps and $\mathcal B$ contains the Coulomb–exchange response kernel, so $C$ is set by their mixed products and RPA mode projections. It cannot be $\omega^3/24$: when $\mathcal B=0$ the Fock matrix is frozen, both propagators are exact and the formula gives $C=0$ for every $\omega$.

### ROUND 4 · OPUS

Sol's Round 3 operator algebra survives in full, and it is now measured rather than asserted: re-derived independently, $\mathcal D_{\rm M2}$ and $\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}$ are right word for word, $\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}-\mathcal D_{\rm M2}=\tfrac14[\mathcal A,\mathcal B]\mathcal L$ holds to $3.1\times10^{-14}$ on an operator of norm $15.5$, its projection on every RPA left/right eigenpair vanishes to $2.7\times10^{-15}$ against a scale of $60.5$, and the no-fit contraction $C_j=-\operatorname{Im}(\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal D r_j)$ reproduces the eigenfrequency error of the actual `lab/density.js` propagators to $0.005\,\%$ on all ten lines — $0.062026$ against Round 2's fitted $0.0620$, and $60.527488$, $53.533582$ against its $60.358$, $53.390$. Four things died. The `eigSym` fix that landed between rounds does not work: $10^{-34}\max(1,\lVert A\rVert_F^2)=8.3\times10^{-32}$ for H₂O's Löwdin Fock sits below the Jacobi rounding floor, so every real-time step still costs mean $93.23$ sweeps with the hundred-sweep cap hit in $185$ of $200$ steps, and B-H2O-3's gate is unreachable as written. Sol's "$\mathcal A^2\mathcal B$ terms" is the wrong word: $\mathcal A^2\mathcal B$ has coefficient exactly zero in both generators, and the carriers are $\mathcal{ABA}$ and $\mathcal{BA}^2$. B-H2O-2's six pinned energies are all correct to $5\times10^{-13}$, but its N₂ gate cannot be met by `lab/scf.js`, which from its core guess converges onto a second, aufbau-obeying RHF solution $0.7298$ hartree above the ground state — and so does PySCF with `init_guess='hcore'`. And Round 2's own $\partial E/\partial R_{\rm sym}=-0.081555843$ is a $\pm0.05$ Å secant, not a derivative; the derivative is $-0.074996516$.

#### 1 · Question 13, the modified generators

**Definition 2 (the linearised problem, and where it lives).** DERIVED-HERE, fixing Sol's Answer 8 in the Löwdin frame the code actually uses. $\tilde F_0=X F[D_0]X$, $P_0=WD_0W$, $[\tilde F_0,P_0]=0$; for a Hermitian increment $M$,
$$ \mathcal AM=-i[\tilde F_0,M],\qquad \mathcal BM=-i\big[\tilde{\mathcal G}(M),P_0\big],\qquad \tilde{\mathcal G}(M)=X\,g\!\left(XMX\right)X,\qquad \mathcal L=\mathcal A+\mathcal B, $$
with $g(D)_{ij}=\sum_{kl}\big[D_{kl}(ij\vert kl)-\tfrac12D_{lk}(il\vert kj)\big]$ — the exchange index order of `lab/density.js`, not the one that is invisible to a real SCF. All three map Hermitian matrices to Hermitian matrices, so each is a real $49\times49$ matrix in the orthonormal Hermitian basis $\{E_{aa}\}\cup\{(E_{ab}+E_{ba})/\sqrt2,\;i(E_{ab}-E_{ba})/\sqrt2\}_{a<b}$. Because $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal B\subseteq$ the occupied–virtual block and $\mathcal A$ preserves every block, the $2n_{\rm occ}n_{\rm vir}=20$-dimensional $ov\oplus vo$ subspace is $\mathcal L$-invariant and carries exactly the ten $\pm i\omega_k$ pairs; the complementary $29$ dimensions are $\mathcal A$-invariant with eigenvalues $-i(\varepsilon_p-\varepsilon_q)$ inside one block and are never excited, because a $\delta$-kick starts the system at $\delta P(0)=-i\kappa[\tilde M_q,P_0]+O(\kappa^2)$, which lies in $ov\oplus vo$. MEASURED ([scratch/lin.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/lin.mjs), [scratch/gen3.py](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/gen3.py)): the twenty eigenvalues of $\mathcal L$ restricted to that subspace reproduce PySCF's ten TDHF roots to $1.09\times10^{-10}$ with $\max\lvert\operatorname{Re}\lambda\rvert=1.4\times10^{-17}$, so $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are built right before a single generator is expanded.

**Lemma 5 (the linearised Magnus-2 predictor–corrector map, closed form).** DERIVED-HERE. With $E=e^{h\mathcal A}$ and $\varphi=\varphi_1(h\mathcal A)$, $\varphi_1(z)=(e^z-1)/z$,
$$ \mathcal M_{\rm M2}(h)=E+\tfrac h2\,\varphi\mathcal B\big(I+E+h\varphi\mathcal B\big). $$
**Proof.** Conjugation by $e^{-ih(F_0+\Delta F)}$ is $e^{h(\mathcal A+\Gamma)}$ with $\Gamma Y=-i[\Delta F,Y]$. Apply it to $P_0+M$ and keep terms linear in the perturbation. Terms with no $\Gamma$ give $e^{h\mathcal A}M$. Terms with exactly one $\Gamma$ act on $P_0$; in $\sum_n\frac{h^n}{n!}\sum_{j}\mathcal A^j\Gamma\mathcal A^{n-1-j}P_0$ every summand with $n-1-j\ge1$ dies because $\mathcal AP_0=-i[\tilde F_0,P_0]=0$, leaving $\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{h^n}{n!}\mathcal A^{n-1}\Gamma P_0=h\varphi_1(h\mathcal A)\,\Gamma P_0$. The predictor has $\Gamma P_0=\mathcal BM$, so $\delta P^\ast=(E+h\varphi\mathcal B)M$; the corrector uses $\tfrac12\tilde{\mathcal G}(M+\delta P^\ast)$, whose $\Gamma P_0$ is $\tfrac12\mathcal B(I+E+h\varphi\mathcal B)M$. $\square$

**Lemma 6 (the unrestarted MMUT recurrence).** DERIVED-HERE. $\delta P_{n+1}=e^{2h\mathcal A}\delta P_{n-1}+2h\varphi_1(2h\mathcal A)\mathcal B\,\delta P_n$, a two-term recurrence whose physical root operator $Z$ solves $Z^2=e^{2h\mathcal A}+2h\varphi_1(2h\mathcal A)\mathcal BZ$.
**Proof.** Identical to Lemma 5 with step $2h$, except that the generator is evaluated at $\delta P_n$ while the conjugation acts on $P_0+\delta P_{n-1}$, so the two dependencies separate. $\square$

**Proposition 10 (Sol's $\mathcal D_{\rm M2}$, confirmed).** DERIVED-HERE. Writing $\mathcal M(h)=\exp(h\mathcal L+h^3\mathcal D+O(h^4))$,
$$ \mathcal D_{\rm M2}=\frac{\mathcal{ABA}+\mathcal{AB}^2+\mathcal{BA}^2+\mathcal{BAB}}{12}-\frac{\mathcal B^2\mathcal A+\mathcal B^3}{6}. $$
**Proof.** Expand Lemma 5: $\tfrac h2\varphi\mathcal B(I+E)=h\mathcal B+\tfrac{h^2}2(\mathcal{BA}+\mathcal{AB})+\tfrac{h^3}2\big(\tfrac12\mathcal{BA}^2+\tfrac12\mathcal{ABA}+\tfrac13\mathcal A^2\mathcal B\big)$ and $\tfrac{h^2}2\varphi\mathcal B\varphi\mathcal B=\tfrac{h^2}2\mathcal B^2+\tfrac{h^3}4(\mathcal{AB}^2+\mathcal{BAB})$. Adding $E$ gives $I+h\mathcal L+\tfrac{h^2}2\mathcal L^2$ at the first two orders — second order, as required — and at $h^3$ the word coefficients $\tfrac16\mathcal A^3+\tfrac14\mathcal{BA}^2+\tfrac14\mathcal{ABA}+\tfrac16\mathcal A^2\mathcal B+\tfrac14\mathcal{AB}^2+\tfrac14\mathcal{BAB}$. Subtract $\tfrac16\mathcal L^3$, whose eight words each carry $\tfrac16$: $\mathcal A^3$ and $\mathcal A^2\mathcal B$ cancel exactly, four words are left at $\tfrac14-\tfrac16=\tfrac1{12}$, and $\mathcal B^2\mathcal A,\mathcal B^3$ at $-\tfrac16$. $\square$

**Proposition 11 (Sol's $\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}$, confirmed).** DERIVED-HERE. $\displaystyle\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}=\frac{\mathcal{ABA}+\mathcal{AB}^2}{3}-\frac{\mathcal{BA}^2+\mathcal{BAB}+\mathcal B^2\mathcal A+\mathcal B^3}{6}$.
**Proof.** Put $Z=I+hz_1+h^2z_2+h^3z_3$ into Lemma 6's root equation with $e^{2h\mathcal A}=I+2h\mathcal A+2h^2\mathcal A^2+\tfrac43h^3\mathcal A^3$ and $2h\varphi_1(2h\mathcal A)\mathcal B=2h\mathcal B+2h^2\mathcal{AB}+\tfrac43h^3\mathcal A^2\mathcal B$. Order $h$ gives $z_1=\mathcal L$, order $h^2$ gives $z_2=\tfrac12\mathcal L^2$, and order $h^3$ gives $2z_3=\tfrac43\mathcal A^2\mathcal L+\mathcal{BL}^2+2\mathcal{ABL}-\mathcal L^3$, so $z_3-\tfrac16\mathcal L^3=\tfrac23\mathcal A^2\mathcal L+\tfrac12\mathcal{BL}^2+\mathcal{ABL}-\tfrac23\mathcal L^3$, which on expansion leaves $\mathcal A^3$ and $\mathcal A^2\mathcal B$ at $\tfrac23-\tfrac23=0$, $\mathcal{ABA},\mathcal{AB}^2$ at $1-\tfrac23=\tfrac13$, and the four $\mathcal B$-led words at $\tfrac12-\tfrac23=-\tfrac16$. $\square$

**Corollary 11.1 (the difference, and why the line positions do not see it).** DERIVED-HERE, confirming Sol. Subtracting, the $\mathcal B^2\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B^3$ terms cancel identically and
$$ \mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}-\mathcal D_{\rm M2}=\tfrac14\big(\mathcal{ABA}+\mathcal{AB}^2-\mathcal{BA}^2-\mathcal{BAB}\big)=\tfrac14[\mathcal A,\mathcal B]\mathcal L=\tfrac14[\mathcal A,\mathcal L]\mathcal L, $$
and for any left/right pair $\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal L=\lambda_j\ell_j^\dagger$, $\mathcal Lr_j=\lambda_jr_j$, $\ell_j^\dagger(\mathcal{AL}-\mathcal{LA})\mathcal Lr_j=\lambda_j^2\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal Ar_j-\lambda_j^2\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal Ar_j=0$. MEASURED: $\lVert\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}-\mathcal D_{\rm M2}-\tfrac14[\mathcal A,\mathcal B]\mathcal L\rVert=3.1\times10^{-14}$ against $\lVert\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}-\mathcal D_{\rm M2}\rVert=15.5$, and $\max_j\lvert\ell_j^\dagger\tfrac14[\mathcal A,\mathcal B]\mathcal Lr_j\rvert=2.7\times10^{-15}$ against $\max_j\lvert\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal D_{\rm M2}r_j\rvert=60.53$.

**MEASURED · the closed forms are the code.** [scratch/lin.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/lin.mjs) extracts the linearised maps of the imported `magnus2` and `mmut` of `lab/density.js` by central finite differences ($\epsilon=10^{-6}$) about $P_0$ in the same Hermitian basis, for $\Delta t\in\{0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025\}$ and response scaling $s\in\{0,\tfrac14,\tfrac12,1\}$. Against Lemmas 5 and 6 the worst disagreement over all sixteen pairs is $2.7\times10^{-8}$ on maps of norm $4.5$, and it does not fall with $\Delta t$ — it is the finite-difference floor, not a discrepancy. The $s=0$ column is the calibration: there the Fock is frozen, both schemes are exact, and the measured $C_j$ is $1.3\times10^{-6}$ instead of $0$.

**MEASURED · unrestarted MMUT, the theory.** The exact $40\times40$ companion of Lemma 6, $\begin{pmatrix}2h\varphi_1(2h\mathcal A)\mathcal B&e^{2h\mathcal A}\\I&0\end{pmatrix}$, splits into twenty physical roots $\zeta\approx e^{-i h\omega_j}$ and twenty parasitic roots $\zeta\approx-e^{+ih\,\cdot}$. At $\Delta t=0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025,0.001$ the largest $\lvert\lvert\zeta\rvert-1\rvert$ is $2.2\times10^{-15},4.0\times10^{-15},2.2\times10^{-15},2.2\times10^{-15},2.0\times10^{-15}$ for the parasitic branch and the same order for the physical one: the parasitic branch is neutrally stable to machine precision at every step size tried, so it can only appear at the amplitude with which it is seeded. The seed is the single Magnus-2 startup step: decomposing $(\delta P_1,\delta P_0)$ with $\delta P_1=\mathcal M_{\rm M2}(h)\delta P_0$ in the companion's eigenbasis gives parasitic/physical $=6.481\times10^{-6},\,7.697\times10^{-7},\,9.439\times10^{-8},\,1.170\times10^{-8},\,7.459\times10^{-10}$ — a clean $\Delta t^3$ law (ratios $8.42$, $8.15$, $8.07$, $15.7$ for the last $2.5\times$). Its frequency is $\omega_{\rm par}=\pi/\Delta t-1.39366$ at all five step sizes, exactly, because the parasitic root's phase is set by $e^{2h\mathcal A}$ and not by $\mathcal L$.

**MEASURED · unrestarted MMUT, the run.** [scratch/mmut-long.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/mmut-long.mjs), $y$ kick $\kappa=10^{-3}$, $\Delta t=0.01$, $T=2000$ ($200{,}000$ steps, $115$ s), `restartEvery: Infinity` against the lab default $50$. Every valence peak agrees between the two to $\le1.7\times10^{-9}$ and the core peak to $2.4\times10^{-7}$; $\operatorname{Tr}P=10.000000000127$ against $10.000000000129$; idempotency defect $1.5\times10^{-10}$ against $4.2\times10^{-10}$ (the unrestarted run is the cleaner one, because it performs one Hermitian diagonalisation per step instead of two); field-free energy drift $-8.0\times10^{-10}$ against $-1.16\times10^{-9}$. A single-frequency fit cannot see the parasitic mode — leakage from the $\omega=0.807$ line into a $200$ a.u. block at $\omega=312.77$ is $1.3\times10^{-7}$, which is larger than the mode — so [scratch/mmut-par.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/mmut-par.mjs) fits all ten lines (shifted by $C_j\Delta t^2$) together with $\omega_{\rm par}$ block by block. Parasitic/physical dipole amplitude: $4.0\times10^{-8}$ at $\Delta t=0.02$ (growth over $50{,}000$ steps, $1.009$), $4.8\times10^{-9}$ at $0.01$ ($1.064$ over $100{,}000$), $6.1\times10^{-10}$ at $0.005$ (ratio $2.2$, at the round-off floor of a $4\times10^{-3}$ dipole). Ratios $8.4$ and $7.8$: $\Delta t^3$, as the seed law predicts, with no growth.

**REFUTED · Sol's Round 1 "the parasitic parity mode … not loss of unitarity, are the risks", and Round 3's "unrestarted MMUT remains the required stability test".** The test has now been run and the mode is not a risk: $\lvert\zeta_{\rm par}\rvert-1\le4\times10^{-15}$ per step and the seeded amplitude is $\Delta t^3$ and constant. Corrected line: a Magnus-2 restart every $50$ steps changes no H₂O peak by more than $1.7\times10^{-9}$ and is therefore merely safe; unrestarted MMUT is both cheaper and slightly cleaner on the invariants. One real hazard survives and is arithmetic, not dynamical: $\omega_{\rm par}=\pi/\Delta t-1.39366$, and because every $\Delta t$ in the ladder divides the output interval $0.02$, $\pi/\Delta t$ is an exact multiple of the output sampling rate $2\pi/0.02=314.1593$, so the parasitic line aliases onto $1.39366$ hartree — between the $z$ lines at $1.0466$ and $1.4617$ — at every step size. Its height is $5\times10^{-9}$ of the strongest line at $\Delta t=0.01$, far under `lab/absorb.js`'s $10^{-4}$ peak fraction, so it is harmless now; it would not be if the output interval were changed to make $\pi/\Delta t$ land inside a window with a weak line.

**MEASURED · the Magnus-2 predictor–corrector is not time-symmetric, yet its frequency error is even in $\Delta t$.** DERIVED-HERE in the sense that the object measured is the exact map of Lemma 5. $(\omega(\Delta t)-\omega_\text{RPA}-C_j\Delta t^2)/\Delta t^4$ is constant to four digits over $\Delta t=0.01,0.005,0.0025,0.00125$ — $-1343.0,-1344.2,-1344.5,-1344.6$ on the $20.157$ line and $-7.89\times10^{-3},-7.88\times10^{-3},-8.50\times10^{-3},\ldots$ on the $0.483$ line — so $\omega(\Delta t)=\omega_\text{RPA}+C_j\Delta t^2+C_4\Delta t^4$ with no $\Delta t^3$ term, even though the predictor–corrector is not a symmetric method. Its $h^3$ generator term is there, and it is purely real: the linearised map is not unitary, $\lvert\lvert\zeta\rvert-1\rvert=5.834\times10^{-6},3.728\times10^{-7},2.343\times10^{-8},1.466\times10^{-9},9.17\times10^{-11}$ at $\Delta t=0.02$ down to $0.00125$ — ratios $15.6,15.9,16.0,16.0$, a clean $\Delta t^4$ — so what the non-symmetry costs is a slow amplitude drift ($\lvert\zeta\rvert^N-1=2.8\times10^{-3}$ over $T=600$ at $\Delta t=0.005$, $3.5\times10^{-4}$ at $0.0025$) and not a line position. That is the mechanism behind one part of the $\epsilon$ of section 3, and it is why Round 2's two-point fits were right.

**REFUTED · Sol's "$\mathcal A^2\mathcal B$ terms amplifying a nonzero response coupling by a squared core gap".** The word $\mathcal A^2\mathcal B$ has coefficient exactly $\mathbf 0$ in $\mathcal D_{\rm M2}$ and in $\mathcal D_{\rm MMUT}$ (Propositions 10 and 11: it cancels against $\tfrac16\mathcal L^3$ in both). Corrected line: the carriers are the two other words that are quadratic in $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal{ABA}$ and $\mathcal{BA}^2$, both at $+\tfrac1{12}$ in $\mathcal D_{\rm M2}$. Their share of $C_j$ is $100.1\,\%$ and $100.2\,\%$ for the two O $1s$ lines, against $-3.6\,\%$/$-4.0\,\%$ for the two-$\mathcal B$ words and $+3.4\,\%$/$+3.8\,\%$ for the three-$\mathcal B$ words; on the valence lines the one-$\mathcal B$ share is $108.6$–$137.0\,\%$ and the two- and three-$\mathcal B$ words are $-70.8$ to $-25.1\,\%$ and $+9.5$ to $+33.8\,\%$. The $s$ scan says the same thing without any word algebra: $C_{10}(s)/s=60.62,\,60.60,\,60.53$ at $s=\tfrac14,\tfrac12,1$ — linear in the response strength to $0.15\,\%$, so the core coefficient is first order in $\mathcal B$ — while $C_1(s)/s=0.0832,\,0.0790,\,0.0620$ spreads by $25\,\%$, so the valence coefficients carry real $\mathcal B^2$ and $\mathcal B^3$ content. So Sol's mechanism is right in substance and wrong in its label, and the discriminating experiment Sol asked for now separates the two regimes quantitatively.

**Proposition 12 (what sets $C$; the answer to question 9).** DERIVED-HERE. Let $a_j:=i\,\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal Ar_j$, the mode-projected occupied–virtual orbital gap. Then $\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal Br_j=-i(\omega_j-a_j)$ and, keeping only the one-$\mathcal B$ words and treating $\mathcal A$ as the scalar $-ia_j$ on the mode's support,
$$ C_j=\frac{a_j^2\,(a_j-\omega_j)}{6}+O(\mathcal B^2). $$
**Proof.** $\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal Lr_j=\lambda_j=-i\omega_j$ and $\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal Ar_j=-ia_j$ give the $\mathcal B$ projection. With $\mathcal A\to-ia_j$, $\ell_j^\dagger(\mathcal{ABA}+\mathcal{BA}^2)r_j/12\to-2a_j^2\ell_j^\dagger\mathcal Br_j/12=ia_j^2(\omega_j-a_j)/6$, and $C_j=-\operatorname{Im}(\cdot)$ is the stated expression. $\square$
**MEASURED.** Ratio closed form / exact: $1.0013$ and $1.0013$ for the two O $1s$ lines ($a_j=20.847002$ and $20.983345$ against $\varepsilon_6-\varepsilon_1=20.847035$ and $\varepsilon_7-\varepsilon_1=20.983461$), and $1.0736$–$1.4136$ for the eight valence lines. This settles question 9: $C$ is not $\omega^3/24$ and not any function of $\omega$ alone; it is one sixth of the squared occupied–virtual orbital gap times the RPA shift $a_j-\omega_j$, and Round 2's $170$–$980\times$ spread of $C$ against a $42\times$ spread of $\omega$ is $(20.98/1.00)^2=440$ from the squared gap times $0.826/0.513=1.6$ from the shift. The a priori timestep rule is $\Delta t\le\sqrt{6\,\text{target}/(a_j^2\lvert a_j-\omega_j\rvert)}$, and it says at once that freezing or projecting out the O $1s$ occupied orbital removes the factor $440$: it is the gap, not the frequency, that costs the seven-fold shorter step.

#### 3 · Question 15, the exact-kernel fit and its certificate

**CERTIFIED · Sol's kernel is exactly `lab/absorb.js`'s transform.** DERIVED-HERE and MEASURED. With $\delta\mu_n=2\kappa\sum_kA_k\sin(\Omega_kt_n)$, $A_k=z_k^2$, `spectrum()`'s output is $\operatorname{Im}\alpha(\omega_r)=\frac{h}{\kappa}\sum_{n\ge1}q^n\delta\mu_n\sin(\omega_rt_n)=\sum_kA_kK_M(\omega_r,\Omega_k)$ exactly, by $\sin a\sin b=\tfrac12[\cos(a-b)-\cos(a+b)]$ term by term — so the amplitude in the kernel is $z_k^2$ with no factor left over, and $I_M$ has the closed form $h\operatorname{Re}\big[z(1-z^{M-1})/(1-z)\big]$, $z=qe^{ixh}$, needing no sum. MEASURED ([scratch/fit.py](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/fit.py)): over $20{,}951$ grid points on $[0.05,21]$ the literal transform of a synthesised trace and $\sum_kA_kK_M$ differ by at most $2.0\times10^{-11}$ against a signal of $97.95$ — relative $2\times10^{-13}$, the accumulation error of the $30{,}000$-term sum, not a modelling gap.

**MEASURED · the fit on noiseless oracle traces, $T=600$, $\tau=50$, $T/\tau=12$.** Ordered poles, NNLS amplitudes, `trf` variable projection; the Jacobian is $[\partial y/\partial\Omega\;\vert\;(\partial y/\partial A)\operatorname{diag}\alpha]$ with $\alpha_k$ equalising the column norms so the frequency block stays in hartree and $4\epsilon/\sigma$ bounds each frequency directly; $L_J$ is the sampled surrogate $\max\lVert J(\theta+d)-J(\theta)\rVert_2/\lVert d\rVert_2$ over five random $d$ of norm $10^{-5}$.

| trace | $\sigma_{\min}(J)$ | $\epsilon$ | $L_J$ | $\sigma^2/(8L_J)$ | $4\epsilon/\sigma$ | worst actual pole error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| four $y$ lines | $64.605$ | $5.04\times10^{-11}$ | $1.61\times10^{6}$ | $3.24\times10^{-4}$ | $3.12\times10^{-12}$ | $1.44\times10^{-15}$ |
| nine bright lines | $29.201$ | $5.34\times10^{-11}$ | $9.19\times10^{5}$ | $1.16\times10^{-4}$ | $7.31\times10^{-12}$ | $1.55\times10^{-15}$ |

Sol's precondition $\epsilon\le\sigma^2/(8L_J)$ holds with seven orders to spare in both, the certificate is $3$–$7\times10^{-12}$, and the actual errors are three orders smaller still, so the bound is valid and conservative rather than vacuous. The contrast the gate needs: on the same noiseless four-line trace the raw parabolic maximum nearest $0.702205382$ sits at $0.704543463$, displaced $+2.3381\times10^{-3}$ — which reproduces Round 2's measurement on a real trace ($+2.336\times10^{-3}$) to $2\times10^{-6}$ and so proves that the whole outlier is the window bias of Lemma 4 and nothing else. Amplitudes come back too: $0.11881213$ against the oracle's $\mu_y^2=0.11881213$.

**MEASURED · the fit on the actual RT trace, and the honest limit.** $y$-polarised Magnus-2, $T=600$, $\tau=50$, output interval $0.02$, the model given the four $y$-bright lines:

| $\Delta t$ | $\kappa$ | $\epsilon$ | $4\epsilon/\sigma$ | raw max error on $0.702205382$ | fitted $-\omega_\text{RPA}$ | $C_j\Delta t^2$ (Q14) | fitted $-(\omega_\text{RPA}+C_j\Delta t^2)$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $0.005$ | $10^{-3}$ | $2.346\times10^{-4}$ | $1.45\times10^{-5}$ | $+2.341\times10^{-3}$ | $+2.463\times10^{-6}$ | $+2.443\times10^{-6}$ | $+1.96\times10^{-8}$ |
| $0.0025$ | $10^{-3}$ | $7.840\times10^{-5}$ | $4.85\times10^{-6}$ | $+2.339\times10^{-3}$ | $+6.267\times10^{-7}$ | $+6.109\times10^{-7}$ | $+1.59\times10^{-8}$ |
| $0.0025$ | $10^{-5}$ | $8.316\times10^{-5}$ | $5.15\times10^{-6}$ | $+2.339\times10^{-3}$ | $+5.987\times10^{-7}$ | $+6.109\times10^{-7}$ | $-1.22\times10^{-8}$ |

The answer to Sol's question 15 is therefore: on a noiseless trace, yes — to $1.4\times10^{-15}$, eight orders better than $10^{-7}$; on a real RT trace, no, and the certificate correctly refuses. At $\Delta t=0.0025$ the fit removes the window bias completely (from $2.34\times10^{-3}$ to $6.3\times10^{-7}$, a factor $3730$) but what it then exposes is the propagator's own $C_j\Delta t^2$, and $4\epsilon/\sigma=4.9\times10^{-6}$ is above $10^{-7}$, so the instrument must decline the $10^{-7}$ claim — which is exactly the refusal state B-H2O-6 specifies. Subtract the Q14 coefficient and the pole is right to $1.6\times10^{-8}$: the fit and the modified-generator theory close on each other to $3\,\%$ of a $6\times10^{-7}$ shift. Two further facts. $\epsilon$ does not fall when $\kappa$ falls by $100$ ($7.84\times10^{-5}\to8.32\times10^{-5}$) and the fitted poles move by $<3\times10^{-8}$, so at $\kappa=10^{-3}$ the $O(\kappa^2)$ contamination Round 2 left unmeasured is not the limiting error — it is below $3\times10^{-8}$ in the pole. And $\epsilon$ falls only by $2.99$ when $\Delta t$ halves, not by $4$: the residual is the discrete propagator's departure from a pure sum of sines (amplitude as well as frequency), so a longer or finer run shrinks the certificate slowly. Reaching a certified $10^{-7}$ needs $\epsilon\le1.6\times10^{-6}$, which at this rate is $\Delta t\approx1.5\times10^{-4}$ — three hundred times the cost — whereas the $C_j\Delta t^2$ correction gets there for nothing.

#### 4 · Question 17, the RHF/STO-3G minimum, and a correction to Round 2

**MEASURED · two independent routes to the stationary geometry** ([scratch/geomopt.py](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/geomopt.py), pinned BSE decimals, $C_{2v}$ with O at the origin). Route 1: a two-parameter Newton on $E(r,\theta)$ with central differences, five steps from the ledger geometry. Route 2, independent of both the parameterisation and any finite difference: a nine-coordinate quasi-Newton on PySCF's analytic nuclear gradient.

| | $r_\text{OH}$ (bohr) | $r_\text{OH}$ (Å) | $\angle\text{HOH}$ | $E$ (hartree) | $\max\lvert F_\text{Cart}\rvert$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ledger geometry | $1.809933563$ | $0.957775595$ | $104.4798388^\circ$ | $-74.963023162862$ | $6.143\times10^{-2}$ |
| route 1, $2$-D Newton on $E$ | $1.869714611$ | $0.989410363$ | $100.0268845^\circ$ | $-74.965901217297$ | $1.438\times10^{-6}$ |
| route 2, analytic forces | $1.869712642$ | $0.989409321$ | $100.0268793^\circ$ | $-74.965901217299$ | $3.501\times10^{-12}$ |

The two routes agree to $2.5\times10^{-12}$ hartree — four orders inside the $10^{-6}$ the commission asked for — and to $2.0\times10^{-6}$ bohr and $5.3\times10^{-6}$ degrees. Route 1's residual force of $1.4\times10^{-6}$ is the honest cost of a finite-difference Newton: the energy is flat to $10^{-12}$ there but the force is not zero to better than $10^{-6}$, which is why route 2 is the one to quote. Symmetric-stretch curvature at the minimum, Richardson-extrapolated from steps $0.02,0.01,0.005$ bohr ($1.247234202$, $1.246972424$, $1.246906993$): $\partial^2E/\partial R_\text{sym}^2=1.246885$ hartree/bohr$^2$. The values $0.9894$ Å and $100.03^\circ$ agree with the STO-3G geometry standardly quoted in the literature; the primary citation is UNVERIFIED here.

**REFUTED · Round 2's own $\partial E/\partial R_\text{sym}=-0.081555843$ hartree/bohr.** Round 2 writes "central difference $\partial E/\partial R_\text{sym}=-0.081555843$ hartree/bohr" from $E(\pm0.05\,\text{Å})$. That is a secant over $\pm0.0944863$ bohr, not a derivative: the central difference at steps $0.0944863$, $0.0377945$, $0.0188973$, $0.002$, $0.001$ bohr gives $-0.081555843$, $-0.076041424$, $-0.075257580$, $-0.074999439$, $-0.074997247$, and PySCF's analytic gradient projected on the symmetric stretch gives $-0.074996516$. Corrected line: the generalised force at the ledger geometry is $+0.074996516$ hartree/bohr toward longer O–H bonds, and the wide secant overstates it by $8.7\,\%$ because $\partial^3E/\partial R^3\approx4.4$ hartree/bohr$^3$. The sign, and hence Round 2's and Round 3's conclusion, is unaffected; the number is not. Largest Cartesian force at the ledger geometry: $6.143\times10^{-2}$ hartree/bohr, on a hydrogen.

**REFUTED · B-H2O-2's N₂ gate, as reachable by the named module.** Sol writes "`tests/rhf-molecules.test.mjs` must reproduce pinned-BSE energies … $-107.495887883412$ … to $10^{-9}$", with `lab/rhf-molecules.js` and `lab/scf.js` as the modules. `lab/scf.js` cannot do it, and the failure is not its algebra. MEASURED ([scratch/n2probe.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/n2probe.mjs), [scratch/n2saddle.py](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/n2saddle.py), [scratch/n2iter2.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/n2iter2.mjs)): every option — `diis` $\in\{0,2,4,8,20\}$, damping $\in\{0,0.5,0.8\}$ — converges to $-106.766097415129$, and that point is a genuine, aufbau-obeying RHF stationary point ($\lVert X^\intercal(FDS-SDF)X\rVert_\infty=5.9\times10^{-13}$, $\operatorname{Tr}(DS)=14.000000000000$, its own $\varepsilon$ in ascending order) whose $\pi_u$ degeneracy is broken ($-0.642536,-0.606615$ where the ground state has $-0.572999$ twice). It is reached because `lab/scf.js` has only the bare core-Hamiltonian guess: PySCF with `init_guess='hcore'` returns the same $-106.766097415128$ and reports `converged=True`, while `minao` and `atom` both return $-107.495887883412$. It is a marginally unstable fixed point of the Roothaan map, and which eigensolver you use decides whether you leave it: driven by `lab/h2ci.js`'s Jacobi solver the plain iteration sits there for $200$ cycles at $\lVert e\rVert_\infty=2.4\times10^{-14}$, while LAPACK's `eigh` on identical integrals leaves at cycle $\sim16$ and lands on $-107.495887883413$ by cycle $50$. Corrected line: the six energies stand, but the contract must add a non-core initial guess (superposition of atomic densities, or a minimal-basis projection) to the module list and must require the test to assert the aufbau-plus-stability property, not only $\lvert\Delta E\rvert<10^{-9}$ — because an RHF number can be converged to $10^{-13}$ and wrong by $0.73$ hartree. It is also the first place in this ledger where a ladder rung fails, and it fails on exactly the rung Sol predicted would "expose multiple bonds".

#### 6 · B-H2O-3: the `eigSym` fix that landed does not work

**REFUTED · the landed stop, and B-H2O-3's gate.** `lab/h2ci.js` now stops on $\text{off}<10^{-34}\max(1,\lVert A\rVert_F^2)$, and the Judge recorded that as the answer to Round 2's $11\times$ tax. It is not. For H₂O's realified $14\times14$ Löwdin Fock, $\lVert A\rVert_F=28.7416$ so $\lVert A\rVert_F^2=826.1$ and the threshold is $8.26\times10^{-32}$ — but the attainable Jacobi floor is between $8\times10^{-30}$ and $10^{-31}$, so the test is essentially never satisfied. MEASURED on the same $200$ H₂O real-time Focks as Round 2 ([scratch/eigsym-gate.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/eigsym-gate.mjs)):

| stopping test | threshold for H₂O | mean sweeps | $100$-sweep caps | worst $\text{off}$ at exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $\text{off}<10^{-34}$ (pre-fix) | $10^{-34}$ | $98.16$ | $196/200$ | $9.98\times10^{-30}$ |
| $\text{off}<10^{-34}\max(1,\lVert A\rVert_F^2)$ (landed) | $8.26\times10^{-32}$ | $\mathbf{93.23}$ | $\mathbf{185/200}$ | $9.98\times10^{-30}$ |
| $\text{off}<(10^{-14}\lVert A\rVert_F)^2$ | $8.26\times10^{-26}$ | $10.24$ | $0/200$ | $8.16\times10^{-26}$ |
| $\text{off}<(10^{-15}\lVert A\rVert_F)^2$ | $8.26\times10^{-28}$ | $11.60$ | $0/200$ | $8.25\times10^{-28}$ |
| $\text{off}<(10^{-16}\lVert A\rVert_F)^2$ | $8.26\times10^{-30}$ | $13.02$ | $0/200$ | $8.21\times10^{-30}$ |

The landed constant removes $6\,\%$ of the excess sweeps, not $90\,\%$: the recommended corrected line is $\text{off}<10^{-30}\lVert A\rVert_F^2$, equivalently $\text{off}<(10^{-15}\lVert A\rVert_F)^2$, which is scale-free, converges in mean $11.60$ sweeps with zero caps, and leaves the fourteen eigenvalues of every one of the $200$ Focks agreeing with the strictest rule to $3.3\times10^{-13}$. **REFUTED · the gate's own number.** Sol pins "a mean $8.7$ sweeps with zero $100$-sweep caps". Even with the correct rule today's mean is $10.24$, and Round 2's script rerun unchanged now prints $10.2$ and $98.2$ where it printed $8.7$ and $95.9$ — because a sweep count is an integer threshold crossing on a trajectory that the stopping rule itself perturbs at the $10^{-13}$ level, so it is not reproducible to one decimal. Corrected gate: zero $100$-sweep caps, mean sweeps $\le15$, and $\max\lvert\Delta\lambda\rvert\le10^{-12}$ against a reference diagonalisation — a bound and an invariance, not a pinned mean. The nine response roots are unchanged by the choice: the discrete-map eigenvalues of section 2, computed with the landed rule, reproduce PySCF's TDHF roots to $1.09\times10^{-10}$.

#### 7 · Question 16, the 6-31+G\* oracle, and the $R_d$ mutation

**MEASURED · the pinned record.** Fetched from `https://www.basissetexchange.org/api/basis/6-31%2Bg_st_/format/json?elements=1,8&version=1`, which $308$-redirects to `.../format/json/?elements=1,8&version=1`; BSE name `6-31+G*`, version $1$, revision $2018$-$06$-$19$; stored as [research/h2o-2026-09-11/6-31+gs.bse.json](h2o-2026-09-11/6-31+gs.bse.json), SHA-256 `fee4f992bf8fe6a319350ff03a253d77004110eed0d34013b2af1fade4a71ac4`. Oxygen carries five shells in this order — $s(6)$, $sp(3)$, $sp(1)$, $d(1)$, $sp(1)$ diffuse — so the diffuse shell comes after the polarisation shell in the record and any reader that assumes monotone angular momentum will mis-order it. Counts: O $1+4+4+6+4=19$, H $1+1=2$ each, total $\mathbf{23}$ Cartesian AOs, exactly Sol's number.

**MEASURED · the oracle** ([scratch/b631.py](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/b631.py), PySCF 2.14.0, ledger geometry). $\texttt{cart=True}$: $23$ AOs, $E_\text{nuc}=9.189533762935$, $E_\text{RHF}=-76.017441376748$, $\varepsilon_{1\ldots5}=(-20.581085,-1.357115,-0.722148,-0.584954,-0.509261)$. First five singlet RPA roots and oscillator strengths: $0.340631788$ ($f=0.063156$, $x$), $0.416982421$ ($f=0$, dark), $0.431215135$ ($f=0.133041$, $z$), $0.483700036$ ($f=0.029308$, $x$), $0.501440189$ ($f=0.003084$, $z$). The Cartesian $d$ self-overlaps are $2.513274123=4\pi/5$ for $xx,yy,zz$ and $0.837758041=4\pi/15$ for $xy,xz,yz$, confirming Sol's $R_d$ to nine digits. Worth pinning beside it: the spherical basis is a different model, not a different normalisation — $22$ AOs, $E=-76.016256970179$, first root $0.342163674$, so Cartesian and spherical 6-31+G\* differ by $1.18\times10^{-3}$ hartree and $1.5\times10^{-3}$ in the first root, and a saved project must say which it used.

**MEASURED · $l=2$ is already in the engine, and it holds.** `md.mjs` has carried $l\le2$ since Round 2 but was tested only on one three-shell fixture. Run on this basis ([scratch/b631.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/b631.mjs)) it builds all $23^4$ ordered ERI quartets in $893$ ms and, through `lab/scf.js`, returns $E=-76.017441376748$: $\lvert\Delta\rvert=2.8\times10^{-14}$ against the oracle. Its own superoperator RPA roots ([scratch/b631b.py](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/b631b.py), the $180$-dimensional $ov$ block of a $90$-pair problem) match PySCF's TDHF to $1.0\times10^{-8}$ and the five oscillator strengths to $1.9\times10^{-7}$ relative. So the answer to the first half of question 16 is yes, and no $l=2$ work is needed. One honest caveat: $\max\lvert\Delta\varepsilon\rvert=1.6\times10^{-8}$ where STO-3G gave $5\times10^{-12}$, and the energies still agree to $10^{-14}$ — the variational energy is quadratic in the density error while $\varepsilon$ is linear, so $\Delta E\approx(\Delta\varepsilon)^2$ is the signature of one of the two SCFs being converged only to $10^{-8}$ in the density, not of an integral defect ($\operatorname{cond}S=306$ here against $5.6$ for STO-3G).

**MEASURED · the $R_d$ mutation, which turned out to be cheap.** RHF is invariant under any invertible rescaling of the AO basis, so omitting the $R_d$ congruence on $S$, $T$, $V$ or the ERI breaks the ground state — for the overlap class, $\operatorname{Tr}(DS)$ moves from $10.000000000000$ to $10.077920588738$ — and is caught by a two-line check. There is exactly one class whose omission is invisible to every ground-state scalar: the dipole/position class, which enters no energy, no orbital eigenvalue and no RPA root. Mutating only that one, $M\mapsto R_dMR_d$ with $R_d=\operatorname{diag}(\ldots,\sqrt{4\pi/5},\sqrt{4\pi/15},\ldots)$ on the six $d$ components, leaves $E$, all $\varepsilon$ and all $90$ roots bit-identical and moves the oscillator strengths by $+20.62\,\%$, $+11.87\,\%$, $+34.43\,\%$ and $+61.31\,\%$ on roots $1$, $3$, $4$ and $5$. That is the mutation Sol asked for, and it answers question 10's "smallest test" as well: the smallest test that catches a $d$-normalisation slip in a spectrum rather than in an overlap diagonal is an oscillator strength, because for every other tensor class the overlap diagonal already catches it.

#### 8 · The eight build contracts, judged

1. **B-H2O-1 — gate ill-posed in form, numbers real, and now strengthened.** "Must reproduce H₂O's worst $V$ difference $5.2\times10^{-14}$ … and the Boys worst relative error $7.19\times10^{-16}$" asks a test to reproduce two rounding residues, which are build-, library- and order-of-summation dependent. Corrected: assert $\max\lvert\Delta V\rvert\le10^{-12}$ and Boys relative $\le10^{-14}$ (Round 1's own acceptance rule) and record the achieved $5.2\times10^{-14}$ and $7.19\times10^{-16}$ as regression baselines. The $d$ overlaps are real and re-measured here: $4\pi/5=2.513274123$, $4\pi/15=0.837758041$. Add the stronger $l=2$ gate the engine already passes: H₂O/6-31+G\* at `cart=True`, $23$ AOs, $E=-76.017441376748$ to $10^{-12}$, against the vendored record with SHA-256 `fee4f99…`.
2. **B-H2O-2 — all six numbers real; the N₂ gate unreachable by the named modules.** See section 5. Corrected: add a non-core initial guess to the module list, pin the NH₃ and CH₄ Cartesian placements given above (the energy is placement-invariant but a fixture is not), and make the assertion aufbau and stability, not only $\lvert\Delta E\rvert<10^{-9}$.
3. **B-H2O-3 — gate not met by the landed code and not reproducible as written.** See section 6. Corrected: stop on $\text{off}<10^{-30}\lVert A\rVert_F^2$; gate on zero caps, mean sweeps $\le15$, and $\max\lvert\Delta\lambda\rvert\le10^{-12}$.
4. **B-H2O-4 — every number real; one missing "must not claim".** Re-measured with the converged $D$ ([scratch/gates.mjs](h2o-2026-09-11/scratch/gates.mjs)): $96^3=884{,}736$ voxels, $7\times884736\times4=24{,}772{,}608$ bytes, $\rho(\mathrm O)=193.313905$ ($\Delta=5.0\times10^{-6}$ against Sol's pin), $\rho(\mathrm H)=0.362710$ ($\Delta=9.5\times10^{-6}$), $\rho$ at the O–H midpoint $0.492165$, $\rho=1.8010\times10^{-28}$ twelve bohr out. Add: the contract must not claim the display grid is a quadrature. A midpoint sum of $\rho$ over $96^3$ on the $\pm10.3$ bohr box gives $9.662692$ electrons, $3.4\,\%$ short; on a $\pm24$ bohr box $8.600860$; only $192^3$ on the tight box reaches $9.984107$. The O $1s$ cusp is unresolved at any display resolution, so $\operatorname{Tr}(DS)$ must never be validated on the field grid.
5. **B-H2O-5 — one gate tolerance wrong.** "$\operatorname{Tr}(DS)=10$ within $10^{-12}$" contradicts Round 2's own measured drift of $1.6\times10^{-15}$ electrons per step: at $120{,}000$ steps the correct value is $10.00000000019$. Corrected: $\lvert\operatorname{Tr}(DS)-N_e\rvert\le\max(10^{-12},\,3n\varepsilon\cdot\text{steps})$, with the step count in the record. Section 1 also promotes the MMUT history from a special case to the default: unrestarted MMUT is cheaper and slightly cleaner, so `P(t−h)` and the parity flag are not an optional branch.

**Questions for Sol.**

18. Proposition 12 makes the seven-fold timestep penalty a squared orbital gap, $a_j^2(a_j-\omega_j)/6$ with $a_j=20.98$, not a frequency effect. Is there a core-projected propagator — the O $1s$ occupied orbital kept in $F_0$ but removed from $\partial F/\partial P$, so the $\mathcal{ABA}$ and $\mathcal{BA}^2$ words lose their large-$\mathcal A$ factor — whose modified generator you can write down, and what is the leading error it introduces in the seven valence lines? If that error is below $10^{-5}$ the instrument gets $\Delta t=5.6\times10^{-3}$ back while still showing the core line that RPA and TDA agree on to $4.6\times10^{-5}$.
19. The Magnus-2 predictor–corrector is not a symmetric method, yet its linearised eigenfrequency error is even in $\Delta t$: $(\omega(\Delta t)-\omega_\text{RPA}-C_j\Delta t^2)/\Delta t^4$ is constant to four digits over $\Delta t=0.01\ldots0.00125$ ($-1344.6$ on the core line), while the $h^3$ part of its generator appears only as non-unitarity, $\lvert\lvert\zeta\rvert-1\rvert=5.834\times10^{-6}\ldots9.17\times10^{-11}$, a clean $\Delta t^4$. Is there a theorem that the $h^3$ term of a predictor–corrector Magnus generator is a pure defect of unitarity — real projection on every RPA eigenpair, no frequency shift — for any Hermitian $F[P]$ and any stationary $P_0$? If so, every even-order claim for this family follows without assuming time symmetry, and the implicit symmetric variant buys only the $O(\Delta t^4)$ amplitude drift ($2.8\times10^{-3}$ over $T=600$ at $\Delta t=0.005$) at the price of an inner iteration per step.
20. In the exact-kernel fit $\epsilon$ falls only as $\Delta t^{1.58}$ ($2.346\times10^{-4}\to7.840\times10^{-5}$), because the discrete propagator's amplitudes are also wrong at $O(\Delta t^2)$. What is the amplitude analogue of $C_j$ — the $O(h^2)$ perturbation of $\ell_j$ and $r_j$ under $\mathcal L+h^2\mathcal D$, contracted with the kick vector and the dipole functional? A $\Delta t$-aware fit model would drive $\epsilon$ to the round-off floor and make a certified $10^{-7}$ on a real trace free instead of three hundred times more expensive.
21. N₂/STO-3G has a second aufbau RHF solution $0.7298$ hartree up, held for $200$ cycles by a Jacobi eigensolver and escaped at cycle $16$ by LAPACK. Is there a diagnostic computable from a converged solution alone — the lowest eigenvalue of the RPA $\mathcal A-\mathcal B$ block, which is the same superoperator this round built and costs one $20\times20$ diagonalisation — that flags a non-minimum without a second SCF, and does it stay cheap through C₂H₄ and C₆H₆?
22. The parasitic MMUT line sits at $\pi/\Delta t-1.39366$ at all five step sizes, a constant offset that is not any RPA root and not any orbital gap; the leading-order argument from $\zeta_+\zeta_-=-\text{eig}(e^{2h\mathcal A})$ predicts $\pi/h-(2a_j-\omega_j)$, whose minimum over the ten modes is $1.516$, not $1.394$. What is the exact expression? It matters because every $\Delta t$ that divides the output interval aliases the line onto that offset exactly, and here it lands at $1.39366$ hartree between two real $z$ lines.
23. Cartesian and spherical 6-31+G\* are different models, not different normalisations: $-76.017441376748$ against $-76.016256970179$, and first roots $0.340631788$ against $0.342163674$. The Cartesian set is what the engine does exactly; the spherical set is what published numbers mean. Which should ship as "6-31+G\* water", and should the saved record carry both hashes so a project can be replayed under either?

#### Decisions taken by the lead

1. **Cartesian ships.** The engine, the vendored records and the oracle are Cartesian with per-component unit self-overlap; PySCF cart=True is the oracle; the saved record declares `kind: cartesian`, the component order `s; x,y,z; xx,xy,xz,yy,yz,zz`, and $R_d$ for interoperation. Spherical 6-31+G* is a different model (22 AOs, $-76.016256970$) and is not shipped.
2. **Unrestarted MMUT is the default integrator on screen**, Magnus-2 the startup and the reference; the record carries $P(t-h)$ and parity. The aliasing hazard at $\pi/\Delta t - 1.39366$ is stated in the module header.
3. **Timestep on screen**: $\Delta t = 0.01$ a.u. for STO-3G first-row molecules ($\theta = 0.21$ on the core gap), with the $C_j\Delta t^2$ correction of Question 14 displayed beside any fitted pole, never silently applied.
4. **Peaks are fitted poles, not maxima**, with the $4\epsilon/\sigma$ certificate and a refusal state; the raw maximum is shown as the uncertified reading.
5. **Two RHF solutions are a feature to detect, not a bug to hide**: the molecule module runs a non-core guess and asserts aufbau and stability; a converged second solution is reported by name.
6. **The display grid is not a quadrature**; the electron count shown comes from $\operatorname{Tr}(DS)$, never from the voxel sum.
7. **Geometry role is recorded**: `experimental-fixed` by default; `model-equilibrium` computed and hashed separately before any nuclear motion.

Benzene: $E = -227.891006464$ on 36 Cartesian AOs, bright RPA pair 0.360792 ($f = 0.8127$), on screen. The integral rewrite (shell-pair tables, unique-quartet contraction, primitive screening with proved bounds, Boys by Taylor grid) took benzene's integrals from 40.06 s to 0.561 s with the fixtures unchanged to $10^{-15}$; measured fact for the corpus: shell-quartet Schwarz screening removes nothing on benzene/STO-3G at $10^{-15}$ (42,486 of 42,486 survive). Open after the build: Jacobi at $n = 72$ leaves idempotency $8\times10^{-8}$ after 400 MMUT steps (open problem 8: a Householder–QL Hermitian solver); `moleculeRHF` on benzene is 5.6 s of SCF and stability Hessian, the next cost to cut (open problem 9).

### JOSH'S QUESTION (2026-09-12) · arg for molecules, bulb harmonics, and a compiler — the lead's answer

Commissioned by Josh: "How can I get arg into molecules? Can we take advantage of non-spherical harmonics and go for more general bulb harmonics than relying on 'taylor orbitals'? … there must be some dynamics or easy quick math we can take advantage of. Some kind of compiler to handle hard molecular requests." Written by Claude Fable 5.1.

**Observation 1 (where the phase went).** A closed-shell ground state is one determinant; its density $\rho = \sum_{\mu\nu} D_{\mu\nu}\chi_\mu\chi_\nu$ is real and has no argument, and even the real-time density matrix $D(t)$, though complex Hermitian, gives a real $\rho(\mathbf r, t)$. The phase lives one level down, in the one-electron amplitudes. KNOWN.

**Proposition 1 (the honest arg for a molecule).** Let $\varphi_k = \sum_\mu C_{\mu k}\chi_\mu$ be the canonical orbitals with energies $\varepsilon_k$. A one-electron state $\psi(\mathbf r, t) = \sum_k c_k e^{-i\varepsilon_k t}\varphi_k(\mathbf r)$ is exactly hydrogen's register with the molecule's ladder in place of $-1/2n^2$: it carries $\arg\psi$, it beats at the orbital gaps $\varepsilon_a - \varepsilon_i$, and a HOMO + LUMO superposition is the frozen-orbital (Koopmans) picture of the first excitation. What it is not: the RPA excitation, which is $\omega = \sqrt{(\Delta\varepsilon + 2K - J)^2 - K^2}$ (this ledger, Theorem 2 of the ports); the register beats at $\Delta\varepsilon$ and must say so on its label. The field already presents complex amplitudes; the kernel needs the imaginary AO vector beside the real one. This is the ORBITALS window. DERIVED-HERE from the definitions.

**Observation 2 ("taylor orbitals").** STO-3G is not a Taylor series. It is Hehre, Stewart and Pople's least-squares fit of a Slater orbital $e^{-\zeta r}$ by three Gaussians (1969) — a compiler from the physically right cusped function to the integrable one, chosen because every integral of Gaussians has a closed form (this ledger, round 1). The price is the cusp and the tail; the payment is the two-electron tensor in 0.56 s for benzene. KNOWN.

**Proposition 2 (the bulb harmonics exist, and the tree already owns two of them).** (a) Coulomb Sturmians $S_{nlm}(\mathbf r) = R_{nl}(2\lambda r)Y_{lm}$ with one common exponent are a complete set with the right cusp and a Slater tail; `lab/sturmian.js` and `lab/twocentre.js` already evaluate their exact two-centre integrals in prolate coordinates. Avery's generalised Sturmians extend them to many centres with hyperspherical harmonics; the many-centre two-electron integrals are the open cost. (b) Prolate spheroidal harmonics are the exact separable "bulbs" of any two-centre problem (H₂⁺ is solved in them without any basis). (c) Numerical atomic orbitals (FHI-aims, Siesta): a radial function on a grid times $Y_{lm}$, shaped by the atom's own potential — as cusped as one likes, and integrable only numerically. (d) Multiresolution grids (MADNESS, MRChem): adaptive multiwavelets that refine where the density is sharp — the closest thing to "a compiler that handles a hard request": the basis is generated by the request. On a consumer GPU the operator applications are the cost, not the basis. KNOWN, with the tree's two instances DERIVED-HERE in earlier rounds.

**Proposition 3 (the compilers that exist).** Three things people mean by "compile the hard molecular request": (i) density fitting (RI): replace $(\mu\nu\vert\lambda\sigma)$ by $\sum_{PQ}(\mu\nu\vert P)(P\vert Q)^{-1}(Q\vert\lambda\sigma)$ with an auxiliary basis — $O(N^3)$ instead of $O(N^4)$ and the reason large molecules are routine; (ii) semi-empirical tight binding (GFN-xTB, DFTB): the integrals are replaced by parametrised tables, benzene in milliseconds, the honesty in the label; (iii) the screening we already do (Cauchy–Schwarz bounds with proved errors) — which on benzene/STO-3G removes nothing at the shell level (round BUILD), so the cheap wins are (i) and (ii). KNOWN.

**Decision for the instrument.** Now: the ORBITALS register (Proposition 1) gives arg to every molecule the card can solve, with the label "frozen orbitals · beats at Δε, not at ω_RPA". Next: an RI-J Fock build (Proposition 3.i) if the SCF, now the dominant 5 s of benzene, is to fall further; then a Sturmian or NAO valence basis as the "bulb" rung, gated exactly as STO-3G was. A research round for Sol and Opus: (Q24) the smallest auxiliary basis for which RI-J reproduces the benzene RHF energy to $10^{-6}$; (Q25) whether a one-exponent Sturmian set on each centre can reach STO-3G's benzene energy with fewer functions, and what its two-electron integrals cost with the prolate quadrature already in the tree; (Q26) whether a natural-orbital phase of the real-time density matrix (the eigenvectors of $D(t)$ are complex) is a meaningful arg for a many-electron run, or only a coordinate artefact.
